findings.issue: Spec 5 says the RangeErrors are checked in a fixed order, but each malformed case breaks only one invariant (except [], which also has zero users). If the user-count check were moved after the style check, or the shape checks after seatLineUp's size/preset checks, or the button check before seat resolution, no test would fail.
findings.evidence: Cases: [user(1),bot(3)], [bot(2),user(1)], [bot(1),bot(2)], [user(1),user(2)], null style/name with one user, 11 valid seats, preset 'Custom' with valid seats, bad button with valid seats. None combines two faults.
findings.fix: Add a few combined-fault cases: [bot(1) with style null, bot(2)] -> user-seat message; 11 seats with one bot style null -> style-and-name message; [] with preset 'Custom' -> numbering message; lineUpSessionConfig({...DEFAULT_SESSION_CONFIG, button: 0}, 'Mixed', []) -> numbering message.

findings.issue: lineUpSessionConfig finds the user seat again with seats.find(...) and a cast, after checkedUserSeat already found it inside resolveLineUpName.
findings.fix: Optional: read it from the built seats (sessionSeats.find) or accept the small repeat; there is no behaviour issue.

summary: Both functions match spec 5 and R-1/R-2. The name is compared only against the chosen preset (D-1), names are ignored (A-2), the button is checked after the seats and never clamped (A-4), inputs are not mutated, and only type imports are used. The acceptance tests cover AC#1 at user seat 1, AC#2 with every preset x size 2-10 x every user seat (162 combinations, count checked), AC#3 edit-then-revert, and AC#4 as an exact toEqual. The unit tests cover the default seat 5 case, Mixed edited into the Soft pattern, the Tough/Mixed heads-up case, the sit-and-go base with no stake key, and every RangeError message. tests/bots/lineup.test.ts on its own gives src/bots/lineup.ts 100% statements, branches, functions and lines (42/42, 46/46, 12/12, 33/33). Acceptance tests pass 4/4. The only findings are MINOR: the order of the error checks isn't pinned by any test, and the user seat is looked up twice.
